messages:
maria: noticed a steady spike of 429s and queue growth on dedicated reserved pool sp-42 (eu-west-2) starting 09:03UTC. P99 token latency jumped, several enterprise tenants seeing aborts. tagging @oncall.

raj: confirming, seeing queue_depth -> 540 and admitted_rps down ~45%. Cloud metrics show node GPU util ~98% on that pool.

leah: which tenants are hit? any high-weight customers consuming extra?

maria: primary hit is tenant:alpha and tenant:analytics-batch. Looks like a mix of short chat and long-streaming jobs overlapping.

kevin: ops-bot alert fired: "reserved-pool-admit-ratecap" at 09:05UTC. Repeats every 30s.

ops-bot: alert: reserved-pool sp-42 admission_rate < target (0.62) — backpressure active. See /alerts/12345

sam: quick triage: are there recent rollouts to that pool? deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: deploy: rollout completed for model-qa-v2 to eu-west-2/sp-42 at 08:58UTC by @ci. No errors reported during deploy.

raj: could be sudden workload shift + large streaming jobs not using KV cache. Suggest 1) enable temporary per-tenant soft caps 2) move batch jobs to other pools 3) enable quantized fallback for non-critical tenants.

leah: can we bump autoscale? Pool is at max nodes per AZ, but we have spare capacity in eu-west-1. Cross-AZ move will increase latency but avoid failures.

maria: trying quick mitigations now: will evict low-priority batch jobs and flip quantized fallback for tenant:analytics-batch.

maria: running command to evict low-priority jobs:```bash
redwoodctl jobs cancel --pool sp-42 --filter "priority:low AND tag:batch"
```

kevin: started soft caps for tenant:alpha and tenant:analytics-batch (50% of their usual rps). Notified their owners.

sam: toggled quantized-fallback for analytics-batch:```bash
redwoodctl pool config update sp-42 --fallback-model gptq-7b-q4_0
``` - reducing per-token GPU time.

raj: routing adjustment proposal: route new streaming sessions to hosted fallback for interactive users only, keep batch on dedicated until backlog drained. Who owns routing change?

leah: I can apply a temporary routing policy for the next 2 hours. Will patch traffic split 80/20 (dedicated/hosted) for interactive.

maria: after evictions + caps + fallback: queue depth down to 160, admitted_rps back to 0.88 of target, 429s reduced. P99 latency still higher but trending down.

kevin: customers alpha reported degraded UX but no aborts after caps. Monitoring for error spikes.

ops-bot: recovery alert: reserved-pool sp-42 admission_rate >= target at 09:24UTC.

sam: follow-ups: 1) run backlog drain play to rebalance across eu-west AZs 2) increase pool max_nodes for sp-42 in next maintenance window 3) tighten tenant-weighting rules to avoid single-tenant burst.

maria: filing incident follow-up doc and postmortem. Owners: maria (incident lead), raj (root-cause), leah (mitigation + routing), kevin (customer comms).

leah: temp mitigations left in place: soft caps + quantized fallback + routing split. Removing evictions once backlog < 50.

maria: next steps: schedule capacity review for sp-42, add admission rate early-warning rule (10% deviation) and a playbook entry for cross-region bounce. Also discuss cost impact of adding nodes vs more aggressive per-tenant caps.

kevin: noted — will coordinate comms and estimate cost delta for +2 nodes vs longer-term quota changes.

maria: thanks team. closing thread here, will link postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
